targets.old_statement: Practice targets fifty hours with fifteen after sunset and ten in heavier traffic, all recommendation rather than the six-month permit hold, which is a hard rule.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Practice targets fifty hours with fifteen after sunset and ten in heavier traffic, all recommendation rather than the six-month permit hold, which is a hard rule.
targets.statement: Before the road test, DMV states you should have at least fifty hours of practice—including at least fifteen after sunset and a recommended ten in moderate to heavy traffic—whereas a junior learner permit must be held in valid status for at least six months before taking the road test.

targets.old_statement: The point-and-insurance course buys point relief and premium cuts but never satisfies the safe-driving course gate, the single costliest paperwork confusion in the chapter.
targets.old_spoken_statement: The point-and-insurance course buys point relief and premium cuts but never satisfies the safe-driving course gate, the single costliest paperwork confusion in the chapter.
targets.statement: The DMV-certified Point and Insurance Reduction Program can reduce eligible driving-record points and lower base liability and collision insurance rates, but it does not satisfy the Safe Driving Course requirement.

targets.old_statement: Point relief erases up to four points, repeats every eighteen months, and discounts premiums ten percent for three years, a reward program wholly separate from test eligibility.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Point relief erases up to four points, repeats every eighteen months, and discounts premiums ten percent for three years, a reward program wholly separate from test eligibility.
targets.statement: When eligible, the Point and Insurance Reduction Program reduces up to four points from your driving record every eighteen months and qualifies you for at least a ten percent reduction in base liability and collision insurance premiums for three years, without meeting the Safe Driving Course requirement.

targets.old_statement: Motorcycle supervisors stay within a quarter mile of a passenger-free rider, while car supervisors ride in the front seat, two supervision shapes for two vehicle kinds.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Motorcycle supervisors stay within a quarter mile of a passenger-free rider, while car supervisors ride in the front seat, two supervision shapes for two vehicle kinds.
targets.statement: A Class M or MJ motorcycle or moped learner permit or junior license allows no passenger except a supervising driver licensed for the same class, who must maintain general supervision and control within one quarter mile and should ideally keep the rider in sight.
